title: Solidification and stabilization of Cr(VI) contaminated soil by alkaline industrial waste
content:
Abstract

Basic oxygen furnace slag (BOFS), a calcium-rich alkaline industrial waste, can effectively immobilize Cr(III) but shows limited remediation efficacy for Cr(VI)-contaminated soil. In this study, a synergistic remediation system (VC–BCF) combining a BOFS-based composite (BCF, produced from BOFS, carbide slag (CCR), and flue-gas desulfurization (FGD) gypsum) with ascorbic acid (VC) was developed. CCR and FGD synergistically activated BOFS, enhancing hydration and promoting the formation of ettringite (AFt), C-S-H, and C-A-S-H, while VC efficiently reduced Cr(VI) to Cr(III). The remediation performance was evaluated by unconfined compressive strength (UCS) and leaching tests. Under the optimum parameters (60% liquid-to-solid ratio, 0.8% VC, 15% BCF), the 28-day leaching concentrations reached minima of 0.108 mg/L (total Cr) and 0.037 mg/L (Cr(VI)), and the UCS reached 1.47 MPa. A quantitative synergy analysis showed that the VC–BCF combination immobilized Cr far more effectively than the additive prediction of the individual reagents (synergy factor ≈2.3), confirming a significant synergistic interaction between chemical reduction and matrix encapsulation. The Risk Assessment Code (RAC) of the treated soil decreased from 49.34% (high risk) in the untreated soil to 13.84%–14.65% (medium risk), indicating substantially reduced environmental mobility. Mechanistic analyses suggest that Cr immobilization proceeds through Cr(OH)3 precipitation following VC reduction, encapsulation/adsorption by C-S-H/C-A-S-H/AFt, pore filling, and ion exchange; the assignment of isomorphous substitution of Cr(III) for Al(III) in AFt is inferred from indirect evidence and requires direct spectroscopic confirmation (e.g., XPS, XANES/EXAFS, HRTEM-SAED) in future work.
